page: Amazon Web Services m8i.12xlarge is a general-purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. The hardware allocates 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores running at up to 3.9 GHz, backed by 480 MB of shared L3 cache. System memory comprises 192.0 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 RAM, maintaining a consistent 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware acceleration capabilities include Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector instruction sets. The platform provides a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps, contains no bundled local storage, and includes no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight strong memory subsystem bandwidth, recording 195.84 GB/s on large uncached memory reads and 3825.86 GB/s on cached reads. Computational performance is reflected in a Geekbench multi-core rating of 19971.0 and a software compilation score of 52244.0 using Clang. High operational throughput extends to memory-bound and database workloads, where the instance sustains 89.2 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a Passmark database score of 24101.52. In CPU-based machine learning inference, matrix extensions enable small 135M model text generation speeds of 363.97 tokens per second.

Because the instance configuration provides no onboard NVMe storage, persistent and temporary disk operations require attached network storage. The balanced compute and memory distribution, combined with hardware matrix acceleration, offers high resource efficiency for sustained enterprise workloads without requiring dedicated accelerator hardware. It is structured for data-intensive web tiers, distributed cache nodes, enterprise application servers, code compilation clusters, and relational database services.
description: Amazon Web Services m8i.12xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and Intel Xeon 6975P-C architecture. It provides 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores operating at up to 3.9 GHz, supported by 480 MB of L3 cache and hardware support for AVX-512 and AMX instructions. The instance provides 192.0 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory allocation. Baseline network capacity is rated at 22 Gbps. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage for disk operations. Benchmark metrics demonstrate high memory read bandwidth, strong Clang compilation throughput, and elevated transactional speed, reaching 89.2 million Redis SET operations per second. This instance fits enterprise web backends, distributed caching clusters, build pipelines, and relational database environments.
